description: Deterministic process checks for the stackhawk-data-seed skill (caller-driven). The skill probes for the hawk seed-flow capability, runs `hawk perch seed` (preflight), designs data-seed/manifest.yaml from the emitted digest, then validates and finalizes it via `hawk perch seed validate`/`finalize`. The seed METHODOLOGY lives in the skill now, so the agent DOES author the manifest — that is correct, not a violation. Harnesses look for these signals in agent traces, command histories, generated files, or output text.

checks.description: Agent verifies the working directory is a git repo before proceeding (Phase 0.1).
checks.failure_guidance: Seed artifacts and the credentials handoff land in the repo tree — the skill must run inside the intended git checkout, not a random directory.

checks.description: Agent probes that hawk supports the caller-driven seed flow (`hawk perch seed validate --help` and `finalize --help`). If unsupported it PUNTS with an upgrade instruction (hawk >= min version, brew upgrade / download) instead of hand-authoring seed data (Phase 0.2).
checks.failure_guidance: The new seed flow only exists on a recent hawk. If the subcommands are absent the only correct move is to tell the user to upgrade — NOT to hand-author seed data or fall back to an older single-command flow.

checks.description: Agent checks whether a data-seed/ directory already exists and asks the user augment/replace/cancel before overwriting (Phase 0.3).
checks.failure_guidance: Silently overwriting an existing data-seed/ destroys prior human-curated artifacts. The skill must surface the choice.

checks.description: Agent runs `hawk perch seed --events json` (the static pre-flight) and routes on the `done` event's `outcome` — `needs_synthesis` (continue), `no_local_storage` (recurse into resolved upstreams), or `nothing_to_seed` (honest stop) (Phase 1).
checks.failure_guidance: The pre-flight outcome decides the whole run. Ignoring it (or never running it) means the agent can't tell a seedable repo from a gateway from a no-op.

checks.description: When the outcome is `needs_synthesis`, the agent AUTHORS data-seed/manifest.yaml from the digest (minimal, FK-ordered, idempotent, v1 schema). This is now correct behavior — the methodology lives in the skill. (Inverts the old stub's do-not-handauthor prohibition.)
checks.failure_guidance: The skill's whole job in the needs_synthesis case is to design the manifest. Refusing to author it (or expecting the CLI to synthesize it) is a failure under the caller-driven model.

checks.description: Agent validates the drafted manifest with `hawk perch seed validate <manifest>` (fixing reported errors) and then writes artifacts with `hawk perch seed finalize <manifest>` (Phases 3-4).
checks.failure_guidance: validate + finalize are the deterministic steps the CLI provides. Skipping validate (finalizing an unchecked manifest) or skipping finalize (no artifacts written) breaks the contract.

checks.description: On `nothing_to_seed` the agent relays the honest no-op; on `no_local_storage` it routes to the resolved upstream repos (and reports unresolved ones) rather than fabricating local seed records.
checks.failure_guidance: A storage-less gateway has nothing local to seed — fabricating fake entities to look productive is a failure. The honest outcome (or upstream routing) is correct.

checks.description: On success the agent reports what was written (data-seed/ + manifest.yaml + .data-seed-credentials.env) and the next steps, including that hawkscan consumes the credentials env (Phase 5).
checks.failure_guidance: Without the handoff summary the user doesn't know what was created, what to commit, or how to continue to hawkscan.

checks.description: Agent does NOT write or modify stackhawk.yml — that boundary belongs to the hawkscan skill (Boundaries section).
checks.failure_guidance: stackhawk.yml is hawkscan's domain. Writing it from this skill violates the contract and may stomp on user/hawkscan config.

checks.description: Agent does NOT run docker-compose up, npm start, or any app-startup command itself — starting the environment is the human's job (the skill does not run the artifacts).
checks.failure_guidance: The skill orchestrates `hawk perch seed`; it does not start the user's application stack.

checks.description: Agent does NOT git-add .data-seed-credentials.env (it must remain gitignored and uncommitted).
checks.failure_guidance: Adding the credentials file to git publishes plaintext test credentials.

checks.description: Skill only fires when the user explicitly asks for it — never as an autonomous post-code-change action.
anti_patterns: I'll seed data after each fix
checks.failure_guidance: Unlike hawkscan, this skill is explicitly NOT autonomous. Treating it as a per-commit safety net wastes the user's time and dirties their tree.
